output:
Passes the project's own slopwatch gate. Swap the version number, hex, and feedback path for your real ones.

---

# Dark mode, finally

We shipped dark mode this morning. It took longer than it should have, and the reason is worth a paragraph.

The easy version is a color inversion: flip the background to near-black, flip the text to white, ship it Friday. We tried that in March. Everyone hated it. Pure white on near-black makes thin letterforms bloom and smear, especially on OLED phones, and half the beta group said their notes looked like they were vibrating.

So we started over. Body text is now a soft gray rather than white. The background sits at #16181C: dark, but not the void, with enough tone left that the shadows under cards still read as shadows. Code blocks, search highlights, and the six note colors were remapped by hand instead of run through a filter, because a desaturated yellow highlighter over dark gray turns into mud.

A few things you will notice:

- It follows your system setting by default. If you would rather it switch at sunset, that is under Settings, then Appearance.
- Images and scanned PDFs stay untouched. Nobody wants an inverted photo of a receipt.
- Exports stay light. Your notes still print on white paper.

Dark mode is live in 3.2 on iOS, Android, and web. Desktop lands next week.

If something looks wrong to you, a white flash on launch, a color that fights the background, send us a screenshot from Settings, then Send Feedback. We read all of them.

---

248 words. The angle is "here's the decision we got wrong first," which gives the post something to say beyond the feature existing — if your team never shipped a bad first cut, that middle section needs a different true story.
